reports.reading_scope: Read the entire official SIAM mathematical body, sections 1-7, with relevant footnotes and bibliography. Independently checked selected statements and proof passages in four primary papers on planar domains, dynamics, singly periodic surfaces, and area growth. Every main report branch has an atomic entry or a linked foundation; research proofs remain explicitly cited rather than reconstructed.

proof_scope.2P01: Proves proper Euclidean immersion implies completeness of its induced metric by a Cauchy sequence, compact inverse image, and local metric comparison. Reuses immersion, proper map and metric completeness definitions.
proof_scope.2P02: Defines noncompact genus as the supremum of capped compact subsurface genera, and finite topology separately. The finite-genus/finite-ends characterization uses the noncompact surface classification theorem; the compact-core handle argument is given directly.
proof_scope.2P03: Defines ends by proper rays and nested complementary components. Proves compact metrizability by finite-level subsequences and diagonalization. The finite-genus annular representative is an application, not a prerequisite of the end definition.
proof_scope.2P04: End ordering and restriction of limit ends to top/bottom are cited. Countability follows explicitly from a countable basis and at most two limit ends; no finite-genus hypothesis is inserted into the cited ordering results.
proof_scope.2P05: Fixes eta=T cross N from the outset, computes its relation to Im(2 partial X), and proves homological flux conservation by harmonicity and Stokes. Scaling is derived; the catenoid flux calculation is reused rather than duplicated.
proof_scope.2P06: Computes the isotropic identity and conformal metric for (g,dh); global existence is supplied by the linked Weierstrass integral theorem with zero real periods and nondegeneracy. The conjugate-period obstruction is explained.
proof_scope.2P07: Computes helicoid first and second fundamental forms, minimality and curvature; proves completeness, properness, embeddedness, one-endedness and infinite total curvature.
proof_scope.2P08: Describes the Riemann family, its normalized flux and topology. Existence, embeddedness and the one-parameter global construction are cited, not reconstructed.
proof_scope.2P09: States Collin's finite-topology, at-least-two-ends theorem and the embedded finite-total-curvature end asymptotics. The theorem proof is not reproduced.
proof_scope.2P0A: Derives the finite-topology genus-zero trichotomy using the cited Meeks-Rosenberg helicoid uniqueness, Collin theorem and Lopez-Ros finite-total-curvature classification.
proof_scope.2P0B: States the nonflat finite-genus one-end asymptotic helicoid result. Plane exclusion and properness are explicit; the analytic asymptotic theorem is cited.
proof_scope.2P0C: States the genus-zero two-limit-end structure and flux-controlled curvature theorem. The uniform flux-only bound is restricted to genus zero; individual bounded curvature for finite genus is handled separately in 2P0J.
proof_scope.2P0D: States exclusion of exactly one limit end in the finite-genus proper class. Provides a proof overview using blow-down analysis and quadratic curvature decay, retaining those steps as research inputs.
proof_scope.2P0E: States the complete proper embedded planar-domain classification and explains its finite/infinite-end routes. The Shiffman extremal deformation and global classification proof are cited research arguments.
proof_scope.2P0F: Defines the Shiffman function with the conformal factor and proves that vanishing yields circles or lines in horizontal sections. The Jacobi identity and linear-Jacobi-field rigidity are cited.
proof_scope.2P0G: Explicitly differentiates v=g'/g to derive the modified KdV equation from the stated Gauss-map evolution. This is a local algebraic calculation, not a global existence theorem for the evolving meromorphic data.
proof_scope.2P0H: Explicitly differentiates the Miura transform u=v'/2-v^2/4, obtains ut=(i/2)(u'''+6uu'), and sets tau=-it/2 for the standard KdV time. All constants and the time normalization are retained.
proof_scope.2P0I: Calculates the first two KdV hierarchy polynomials and defines algebraic-geometric potential. Finite-dimensional Jacobi theory, kernel analysis, global meromorphic evolution and period/embeddedness preservation are research inputs summarized in a proof overview.
proof_scope.2P0J: States the finite-genus infinite-end structure and asymptotic theorem: planar middle ends, two limit ends, bounded curvature, and normal graphs over the same-flux Riemann example with possibly different translations at the two ends. No global genus-independent core-curvature estimate is asserted.
proof_scope.2P0K: Defines periodic quotients and distinguishes topology upstairs/downstairs. Finite topology versus finite total curvature in the specified non-simply-connected flat quotient setting and the end models are cited.
proof_scope.2P0L: States the singly periodic genus-zero Scherk-end classification. Retains the non-special convex unit-edge polygon parameter condition for saddle towers; the Jenkins-Serrin construction and global uniqueness theorem are cited.
proof_scope.2P0M: States the doubly periodic genus-zero Scherk classification and explains the local conjugate-data relation. Global period solving and uniqueness are cited.
proof_scope.2P0N: States the genus-one parallel-end KMR classification, distinguishing a basic four-end quotient from a quotient by a smaller translation lattice. The construction and moduli theorem are cited.
proof_scope.2P0O: Defines minimal lamination, leaves and limit leaves. Separates curvature bounded on each ambient compact set from automatic pointwise smoothness. Compactness and closure claims are referred to research theorems.
proof_scope.2P0P: States limit-leaf stability, using the normal double cover for a one-sided leaf. The positive-Jacobi-function stability calculation uses the linked ground-state identity; production and gluing of a global positive solution remain cited.
proof_scope.2P0Q: Calculates the two radial graphs of shrinking catenoids and their smooth convergence on fixed annuli, together with neck curvature blow-up. Distinguishes the sequence's convergence singularity from a singularity of the limiting lamination.
proof_scope.2P0R: Calculates shrinking helicoid multigraphs, sheet spacing and curvature blow-up along the axis. The limiting foliation itself is smooth across the convergence-singular axis.
proof_scope.2P0S: Defines the local simply-connected condition and states the embedded-disk lamination theorem in expanding balls. Rn tending to infinity and boundary conditions are retained; the deep compactness and singular-set regularity proofs are cited.
proof_scope.2P0T: States the two-column planar-domain limit theorem with local simple connectivity, the non-disk component in B(2), and curvature blow-up in B(1). The Riemann-family scaling is recorded from the report, not independently reconstructed.
proof_scope.2P0U: States the local removable-singularity equivalence with quadratic curvature control. Necessity is explained directly; sufficiency and the Riemannian version are cited research results.
proof_scope.2P0V: Calculates how the metric, second fundamental form and curvature scale. Point selection, compact components, multiplicity-one convergence and properness of the nonflat limit are the cited local-picture theorem.
proof_scope.2P0W: Defines D(M), nonempty invariant subsets, minimal elements and dilation/translation recurrence. Keeps divergence of the translation centers in the definition.
proof_scope.2P0X: States the dynamics theorem with the correct distinction between D(M) invariance and the compact normalized slice D1(M). Proves the minimality-to-recurrence deduction and gives a scaled-helicoid counterexample to D1 invariance; compactness and existence of minimal elements are cited.
proof_scope.2P0Y: Defines intrinsic injectivity radius, allowing infinity, and gives its metric-scaling law. Uses a two-dimensional Riemannian manifold, not the complex-analytic definition of Riemann surface.
proof_scope.2P0Z: States the positive-injectivity-radius lamination closure theorem and the stronger Euclidean properness consequence. Local disk estimates and the global half-space/limit-plane argument are cited.
proof_scope.2P10: States the topology-scale local-picture alternatives: smooth proper limit, parking-garage limit, or singular lamination with locally unbounded genus. Bounded genus excludes the third alternative; no assertion that every limit is a smooth surface is made.
proof_scope.2P11: States the fixed-genus end-number bound for finite-topology surfaces and gives only a surgery/blow-up proof overview. Records the sharper Hoffman-Meeks existence conjecture for more than two ends as a conjecture.
proof_scope.2P12: Combines the cited Tysk index estimate, embedded-end Jorge-Meeks degree formula and fixed-genus end bound. The final substitution is explicit. Negative second-variation directions correspond to positive eigenvalues of J for Q=-integral(fJf), or negative eigenvalues of -J.
proof_scope.2P13: States the finite-genus countable-end embedded Calabi-Yau theorem and earlier properness criteria. Its geometric end-representative and barrier steps are a proof overview; the Baire input is proved in 2P14.
proof_scope.2P14: Proves density of isolated points in the nonempty derived set of a countable compact zero-dimensional metric space using Baire and clopen subsets. Does not infer geometric properness from this topological lemma alone.
proof_scope.2P15: Records the cited structural restrictions on a hypothetical nonproper leaf of a minimal lamination of R3 and distinguishes this question from unrestricted complete embedded nonproper surfaces. Existence remains an open question in the report.
proof_scope.2P16: Derives the regular-radius area-monotonicity identity from harmonic coordinates, divergence and coarea; continuation across critical radii uses the standard integral/coarea argument. Computes catenoid area growth 2pi. Quotes the Meeks-Wolf infinite-symmetry classification, retaining the catenoid alternative.
proof_scope.2P17: Records fixed-positive-genus one-end uniqueness and local uniqueness as open problems in the report. Existing examples and asymptotics do not establish uniqueness.
proof_scope.2P18: States quadratic curvature decay iff finite total curvature for embedded surfaces complete outside the origin with compact boundary. Derives scale invariance and the annular-rescaling implication. Compact-region curvature boundedness is explicitly restricted to proper embedding.
proof_scope.2P19: Proves that the source's ball-interior infimum cannot grow linearly when one fixed core point has finite injectivity radius. Records only the broad growth question; no corrected exact conjecture is attributed to the author.
proof_scope.2P1A: Defines general proper continuous maps by compact inverse images, provides elementary examples, and explains proper rays. This is separate from the proper-immersion completeness proposition.

actual_reading.local_review: Parent reports reading all atomic pages through 2P19, including flux orientation, KdV/Miura constants, singular-set distinctions and D1 non-invariance. Requested proper-map separation, end compactness proof, canonical links, curvature properness hypothesis and index wording are incorporated. Source-level checks are recorded below separately from mathematical proof scope.

terminology.proper: 恰当映射 uses compact inverse images (2P1A); proper immersion implies completeness (2P01), not conversely by definition.
terminology.genus: Finite genus of a noncompact orientable surface is defined in 2P02 from compact genus 0F46; finite topology additionally restricts ends.
terminology.ends: 简单端 is isolated in the end space; 极限端 is nonisolated; 简单极限端 is isolated within the derived end space. End definitions do not require a finite-genus prerequisite.
terminology.flux: For the oriented unit tangent T and surface normal N, eta=T cross N; flux equals Im integral(2 partial X). The normalization used for the Riemann family is (h,0,2pi).
terminology.lamination: 层状结构 means lamination; 叶状结构 means foliation. Convergence singularities are distinguished from nonremovable singularities of the limiting object.
terminology.curvature: Environment-local curvature boundedness means a supremum over the surface in each ambient compact set. It is not a consequence of smoothness without properness.
terminology.dynamics: D1(M) is a compact normalized slice, not generally D-invariant. Minimal elements refer to inclusion-minimal nonempty invariant sets.
terminology.riemannian_surface: 2P0Y says a two-dimensional Riemannian manifold and links 00NI/00NV; complex Riemann surfaces in Weierstrass data link 00FR.
terminology.index: Negative second-variation directions are the positive-eigenvalue directions for J when Q=-integral(fJf).
terminology.candidate_review: Direct foundations requested by the parent were linked. Nontrivial topology is not the indiscrete topology 00E6, and an ambient symmetry group is not the permutation-group entry 00DC. Other candidates already supplied through existing prerequisite links were not mechanically duplicated.
terminology.external_check: Site terminology reused; external Banana Space check unavailable.

reports.question: How do convex-core metric/bending data and conformal/projective data at infinity determine hyperbolic 3-manifolds, and how do volume variations connect them to Teichmuller, WP, universal curve and Lorentz geometry?
reports.reading_scope: Read the complete official SIAM mathematical body, sections 1-5.4, including the universal and Lorentz branches, relevant references, publication date and license. Supplemental papers were read at the specific sections and theorem statements listed below, not in full. The arXiv report source archive was downloaded and partially consulted, not counted as a second complete reading.
reports.coverage_status: 46 atomic notes plus narrative outline. Major branches covered with explicit local calculations and separately identified cited research theorems. No claim of reconstructing all research proofs.

The arbitrary geometrically finite/cusped extension, ideal/hyperideal polyhedra, full grafting symplectic theory, quantum-gravity partition functions, and detailed half-pipe transition geometry are deferred.
Metric uniqueness for quasifuchsian convex cores, AdS convex-core uniqueness, and all-X negative Schottky filling remain open questions in this report.
Lorentz realization and mapping-torus convergence proofs are cited through report/original theorem attribution, not independently reconstructed.

terminology.convex_cocompact: 复用2F08的凸余紧；凸共紧为同义术语。
terminology.hyperbolic: Riemann ambient sectional curvature -1 throughout; real hyperbolic space 1719.
terminology.normal: Smooth compact convex boundary: outward nu, B=+nabla nu, H=tr B, II0=II-HI/2. Reuses 2G03; distinct from the Euclidean -dN convention elsewhere.
terminology.infinity: KS I*=(I+2II+III)/2; BBVPW I-hat=2I*. Fuchsian-zero VR is fixed by the K-surface limit; differing W conventions can differ by a topological constant.
terminology.schwarzian: q_dev=S(dev), q_inv=dev* S(dev inverse)=-q_dev; use q_inv for dVR=-Re integral q mu and horizontal-extremal-length relation. CM theorem uses q_dev.
terminology.beltrami: w_barz=t mu w_z; real cotangent pairing Re integral phi mu dxdy; h'_0=2rho Re(bar mu dz2); tensor contraction factor four.
terminology.WP: 2J0X cotangent norm integral |phi|2/rho dxdy and dual tangent norm integral |mu|2 da; single-side gradient constant 3sqrt(pi(g-1)). No numeric Kahler-potential constant asserted.
terminology.Epstein: BBVPW n points away from complement domain, B_E=-nabla n, H_E=tr(B_E)/2; nu=-n gives H=2H_E and coefficient 1/4 instead of 1/2.
terminology.AdS: 2Q15 defines the quadric; 2Q17 explicitly uses its projective +/- quotient for PSL2R x PSL2R. Spacelike Gauss equation K=-1-det B.

reports.title: Ricci-Flat Metrics on Calabi–Yau Manifolds
reports.copyright: 2026 International Mathematical Union; published by SIAM
reports.question: 固定紧 Kähler 流形的复结构，当 Ricci 平坦度量的 Kähler 类趋于锥边界时，体积、正流、局部光滑几何和 Gromov–Hausdorff 极限分别由什么决定，纤维化与逼近路径又如何影响它们？
reports.reading_scope: Read the entire mathematical body, sections 1–4 and bibliography, of arXiv:2509.25607v2, 24 PDF pages, in consecutive pdftotext ranges; compared all mathematical sections and numbered statements against the official SIAM full HTML. Supplemental original papers were read selectively as itemized below, not in full. The SIAM CC BY 4.0 notice was checked on the official page and independently confirmed by the coordinating agent.

proof_scope.2R01: Ricci-form volume-ratio identity and constancy of a pluriharmonic function on a connected compact Kahler manifold proved using Stokes. Chern-Weil identification is external. Uses rho=-(1/2)dd^c log det g with dd^c=i/pi partial barpartial, hence rho=Ric_standard/(2pi).
proof_scope.2R02: Deduction of the Ricci-flat representative theorem from the dd^c lemma and Yau's general prescribed-positive-volume theorem 2N04; uniqueness uses 2N03. Existence estimates and dd^c lemma are external. Calabi–Yau means compact Kahler with c1(X)=0 in real cohomology, without projectivity, simple connectedness or holomorphically trivial canonical bundle assumptions.
proof_scope.2R03: Constant metric scaling and biholomorphic pullback identities proved directly, including length and volume scaling.
proof_scope.2R04: Openness, convexity and nef approximation established using finite-dimensional representatives, positivity and the dd^c lemma. Analytic nef real classes are distinguished from the existing projective nef line-bundle definition.
proof_scope.2R05: Volume is the top-intersection polynomial, so the collapse/noncollapse dichotomy is proved by continuity. The nef positive-top-intersection iff big theorem is an external Demailly–Paun input.
proof_scope.2R06: Null locus is defined for nef classes. Equality with the non-Kahler locus and a strictly positive current smooth off the null locus are cited only under nef and big hypotheses, correcting the report's omitted big assumption.
proof_scope.2R07: General real nef and big noncollapsing boundary theorem quoted with weak-current, minimal-singularity and local smooth convergence conclusions. Global singular Monge–Ampere existence and estimates are not reproved.
proof_scope.2R08: Sixteen fixed points, exceptional-curve area and preservation of positive top intersection calculated. Kummer resolution geometry and analytic convergence are external inputs.
proof_scope.2R09: Boundedness inheritance from minimal singularities proved by two inequalities and compact upper boundedness. The same comparison definition is used in general pseudoeffective classes; existing 2N07 states its construction in big classes.
proof_scope.2R0A: Transcendental contraction conjecture stated; known dimension and projectivity cases reported with source, not proved.
proof_scope.2R0B: Global potential regularity questions distinguished from smooth convergence off the null locus; known semiample special cases cited.
proof_scope.2R0C: Path-dependent weak-current example quoted from report Theorem 3.1 with construction mechanism. This is not an independently reconstructed dynamical proof.
proof_scope.2R0D: Straight-path Monge–Ampere normalization constant derived by total mass, retaining arbitrary smooth representative alpha and choosing the auxiliary class's Ricci-flat representative.
proof_scope.2R0E: Semiample real class defined by pullback from a normal compact Kahler space; smooth regular base and discriminant separated. Rational/line-bundle semiampleness is not presumed.
proof_scope.2R0F: Restricted tangent exact sequence and Whitney formula prove real c1=0 for smooth fibres. General Ehresmann local differentiable triviality is an external theorem; 1907 supplies only a circle-base special case.
proof_scope.2R0G: Full binomial calculation gives the positive t^(n-m) leading coefficient; vanishing of higher base powers and the zero-dimensional-base case are explicit.
proof_scope.2R0H: Pushforward Monge–Ampere equation specified with normalized total mass and a possibly singular base. Existence, uniqueness and regularity of the canonical base potential are cited analytic results.
proof_scope.2R0I: Global potential bound and local quasi-isometry on compact subsets away from singular fibres quoted from report section 3.3.2, equations (3.4) and (3.5). Constants need not remain uniform at the discriminant.
proof_scope.2R0J: Intrinsic fibre diameter two-sided sqrt(t) estimate derived from metric comparison and compact smooth trivialization; ambient fibre diameter receives only an upper bound.
proof_scope.2R0K: Explicit product metric (1+t)g_B+t g_F, exact product distances, fibre scale and volume computed; GH convergence follows from the independently proved correspondence estimate.
proof_scope.2R0L: Fibrewise Yau solutions normalized and assembled into the semi-Ricci-flat form. Parametric elliptic regularity and dd^c gluing are external inputs; total-space semipositivity is not asserted.
proof_scope.2R0M: Hein–Tosatti smooth collapse theorem quoted in every dimension on compact subsets of the regular locus, for the entire straight-path family. Fixed-background C^k topology is explicit; no general numerical convergence rate is asserted.
proof_scope.2R0N: Quadratic semi-flat potential, exact t-lambda rescaling identity and one-dimensional constant-period example computed. Descent under lattice translations is cited rather than independently calculated; general existence of torus semi-flat geometry is external context.
proof_scope.2R0O: Superpolynomial error after subtracting the base-averaged term quoted in torus or locally holomorphically product cases. The rate of the base average itself remains unspecified.
proof_scope.2R0P: Proof outline only: three rescaling regimes and their limiting spaces. Liouville theorems, collapsing Schauder estimates and the iterative selection argument remain external to these notes.
proof_scope.2R0Q: Fixed versus collapsing tensor and Holder norm scaling calculated on a product. Levi-Civita product connection is reused; no general degeneration estimate is inferred from the model alone.
proof_scope.2R0R: Original Hein–Tosatti Theorem B first correction quoted with its negative sign, harmonic Kodaira–Spencer representatives, zero-mean inverse fibre Laplacians and normalization conversion. Harmonic theory, inverse existence and all remainder estimates are external. The full remainder is not claimed to be o(t^2).
proof_scope.2R0S: Finite-order asymptotic theorem and conjectural order-compatible full expansion separated. Integer-power rates are described as an open problem.
proof_scope.2R0T: Rough nonsemiample K3 limit theorem cited. Eigenclass zero-square calculation is elementary; automorphism construction, rigidity and nowhere-continuous behavior remain external.
proof_scope.2R0U: Conditional deduction of whole-family weak convergence from positive-current subsequence compactness and uniqueness of the current. Compactness, positivity under weak limits and dynamical rigidity are external inputs.
proof_scope.2R0V: Bounded-potential conjecture and reported special cases stated, without identifying bounded potentials with continuous two-form coefficients.
proof_scope.2R0W: Minimal-singularity conjecture for arbitrary paths distinguished from the straight-path subsequential result. Existence of cluster limits with minimal singularities does not itself give uniqueness.
proof_scope.2R0X: Irrational zero-square K3 rigidity conjecture and relevant rationality convention stated; known dynamical cases cited.
proof_scope.2R0Y: GH definition and complete proof of correspondence equivalence. Both directions are supplied, including the cross-space metric, positivity, all mixed triangle inequalities and Hausdorff bound. Isometry-class metric theory beyond this equivalence is not reconstructed.
proof_scope.2R0Z: Exact GH distance to a point equals half the diameter; scaling consequence proved from correspondence distortion.
proof_scope.2R10: Uniform diameter bound and Ricci-nonnegative GH precompactness cited. Conclusion is subsequential compactness, not uniqueness of the limit or a positive diameter lower bound.
proof_scope.2R11: Noncollapse GH completion theorem cited. The general real-class conclusion is separated from homeomorphism and real-codimension-four claims requiring additional semiample/integral hypotheses.
proof_scope.2R12: Report Theorem 4.6 quoted for collapse completion and topology. Original Szekelyhidi theorem is identified as projective with semiample line bundle and ample perturbation, whereas the report states the broader Kahler formulation. Singular base, discriminant and its Hausdorff-dimension bound are explicit.
proof_scope.2R13: Straight-path flat-torus quotient formula proved by the infimum over the lattice, monotone convergence and uniform equicontinuity. Closed-subgroup/torus quotient structure is an external elementary Lie-group input. No arbitrary-path extension is claimed.
proof_scope.2R14: Irrational K3 diameter-collapse conjecture stated for fixed complex structure and unnormalized metrics; it is not a diameter-one degeneration statement.
proof_scope.2R15: Rational nef semiampleness conjecture stated at the class level. Flat twists distinguish a semiample class from an arbitrary line-bundle representative.
proof_scope.2R16: Kahler–Ricci-flow application cited. Initial metric is on the total space X, and the unnormalized standard Ricci form is explicitly distinguished from 2R01's normalized form.
proof_scope.2R17: Smooth-fibration rigidity theorem cited; finite-cover global product conclusion retains projectivity, while local holomorphic triviality applies more generally.
proof_scope.2R18: Independent explicit E^2 integer-automorphism counterexample fully calculated: F_k determinant one, tensor limit nonzero, metric isometry to k^(-2) times the fixed flat metric, diameter tending to zero, and comparison with a straight path retaining E.

source_errata.status: hypothesis restricted using the primary theorem
source_errata.resolution: 2P0C uses genus zero as in 1306.1690v2 Theorem 3.1. For finite genus, 2P0J states individual bounded curvature and end asymptotics from Theorem 8.1, not a uniform bound on all compact cores depending only on horizontal flux.
Use the vector (h,0,2pi), rather than the inconsistent (F_h,0)=(a,0,2pi) notation.
The Miura substitution yields ut=(i/2)(u'''+6uu'). Standard KdV time is tau=-it/2. 2P0G and 2P0H display the calculation rather than silently identifying the two time variables.
2P0L excludes special convex unitary polygons as required by Perez-Traizet Theorem 1.1; convex unitary polygons without this restriction are not the parameter domain.

source_errata.status: invariance correction supported by primary theorem and example
source_errata.resolution: The invariant set is D(M); the normalized compact slice D1(M) need not be invariant. 2P0X gives the scaled-helicoid counterexample and follows 1401.1855v1 Theorem 1.3.
2P10 states the smooth, parking-garage and singular-lamination alternatives in prose, without propagating the malformed subitem numbering.
With J=Delta+|A|^2 and Q=-integral(fJf), negative second variation corresponds to positive J eigenvalues, or negative -J eigenvalues. 2P12 fixes this convention.

An infimum over M intersect B(0,R) cannot exceed cR for all large R if any fixed core point has finite injectivity radius. 2P19 proves this obstruction, records the broad question only, and does not invent or attribute a corrected pointwise/annular/exterior conjecture.

source_errata.resolution: The catenoid has area-growth constant 2pi and must be included. 2P16 calculates this and cites the plane/catenoid/singly periodic Scherk alternatives in Meeks-Wolf Theorem 1 for infinite symmetry.

source_errata.status: Sign/functional mismatch under the explicitly adopted outward normal convention
source_errata.resolution: 2Q0C uses KS 0907.2590v2 §4.2 (4.3)-(4.7): 2V'=integral(H'+1/2<I',II>); W=V-1/4 integral H, W'=1/4 integral(H'+<I',II0>). SIAM's leading negative sign and V+1/2 integral H with trace-free derivative are not imported. Fixed ambient normal variation and Fuchsian outward truncation independently test the choice.

Horizontal Q has Gardiner derivative +2Re integral Qmu, so q_inv gives -1/2 dExt. CM realization remains stated for horizontal q_dev.

source_errata.resolution: 2Q0X follows Giovannini v2: local Lipschitz, smooth off switching, derivative bounds where differentiable, WP Lipschitz. No classical global gradient asserted.

BBVPW v2 Theorem 1.6 proves S=4VR for C5,alpha and S>=4VR for general WP; Theorem 1.7 concerns negative gradient of S. Standard Loewner normalization gives I^L=S/pi. 2Q12-14 retain these qualifications.

source_errata.resolution: Metric realization and K-surface limit are attributed by author and mathematical title through the report; unverified original theorem numbers are not invented. Packet does not claim full reading of those sources.

source_errata: Report Theorem 2.2 omits bigness from the claim of a current bounded below by epsilon omega. A nef class of zero top intersection cannot have such a current. 2R06 retains nef and big, following Collins–Tosatti Theorem 1.1; the null-locus definition itself still allows nonbig nef classes.

Report equation (3.13) prints a positive sign in the first Kodaira–Spencer correction. Original Hein–Tosatti Theorem B equation (1.6), visually checked in the PDF, has a negative sign. 2R0R follows the original and converts i partial barpartial to pi dd^c.

Report Example 4.4's kernel-leaf-closure description does not hold for arbitrary converging flat-metric paths. 2R18 gives a fully explicit counterexample on E^2; 2R13 proves the correct straight-path statement.
Report section 3.3.7 places the initial KRF metric on Y; the flow is on X. 2R16 states the initial metric on X.
In the elliptic K3 discussion, pushforward of the volume form is pi_*(omega^2), rather than the square of pi_*omega. The new base equation uses the correct top-degree pushforward.

Occasional pi/f map-name changes in section 3.3 are normalized to f locally. The original asymptotic small parameter is the exponential of minus the original time variable; writing that time variable as s, these notes use t=e^(-s).
